column1: # ARG reporting tiers for bin/results_summary.py (CARD 4.x names; edit freely and pass with --arg-priority).
# These are pipeline-defined reporting tiers, not a published ranking. The basis column says why each tier 1 rule
# is there: "consistent with WHO BPPL 2024" where its genes give a resistance of the WHO Bacterial Priority
# Pathogens List 2024 (the list was not used to write the rules, and its critical third-generation
# cephalosporin-resistant Enterobacterales, ESBL / AmpC genes, are tier 2 here), "pipeline judgement" otherwise
# (resistance to a last-resort drug, usually on mobile elements). The omics-based risk rank of Zhang et al. 2021
# (Nat Commun 12:4765; Rank I-IV from human association, mobility and pathogen hosts) is a different scheme and is
# not used (roadmap Phase 27a: KPC, vanA and mecA are Rank IV in its current table).
# Columns: match (name = regex searched in the ARO name, family = regex searched in the CARD AMR gene family),
#          pattern, tier, category, note, basis (optional; tier 1 rules).
# Rules are tried top to bottom and the first match wins, so put name rules before the family rule they refine.
# A name rule also wins over every family rule below it: keep genes of a tier 1 family out of the name lists
# (cfr genes match the tier 1 Cfr family rule, not the tier 2 'acquired_other' names), and use one to take a gene
# CARD files under a tier 1 family out of it (NmcR, MecI, kamB, sgm, OXA-1262 / OXA-1263).
# Applied before this table: any ARO with CARD SNP definitions (snps.txt), any "protein variant model" and any ARO
# whose name says "mutant" / "mutation" is tier 4 (mutation_dependent); its resistance_snp_status column says
# whether a known resistance mutation was seen.
# Applied after this table: efflux / reduced-permeability mechanisms and overexpression models are tier 3; anything
# Tiers: 1 = high-concern acquired (carbapenemases, VRE van ligases, mecA/mecC, mcr, tet(X3+), optrA/poxtA, cfr,
# 16S rRNA methyltransferases), 2 = other acquired, 3 = intrinsic, housekeeping, efflux or regulator,
